_comment: Registry for the CONTRACT / STAFFING search lane (see CLAUDE.md 'Contract/staffing lane'). Same entry shape as companies.json / remote_companies.json. These are staffing / recruiting firms whose public job feeds we monitor for CONTRACT roles — their CLIENT roles, which is the point: a staffing firm's feed is a window onto dozens of employers, not just its own internal hiring. The lane reads THIS file (not companies.json), applies the local+US-remote gate (is_local — keeps Utah-local + US-remote, drops other-metro on-site and international remote), and runs each profile with staffing_search:true. Contract-only filtering happens in the fetcher on STRUCTURED data (placement_type / emptype), never on the title. Each firm VERIFIED to return live contract roles before adding (do not guess). fetch_logos.py reads this file too.
_v3_comment: Robert Half added 2026-08-11 after probing its surfaces directly. Its own JSON API (prd-dr.jps.api.roberthalfonline.com/search) returns 403 without a client credential, but the public search page at /us/en/jobs SERVER-RENDERS its full result set into a JS assignment (aemSettings.rh_job_search.initialResults), and that payload is richer than most ATS feeds: full description, real date_posted, employment type, structured pay range, remote flag, canonical apply URL, stable job number. robots.txt allows /us/en/jobs. The `queries` below are what the page actually honors — `city` needs a display-cased city name, `stateprovince` alone is IGNORED, and `remote=yes` works. KFORCE WAS PROBED AND REJECTED: no RSS, no sitemap, no ATS; its Find Work SPA queries an Azure Cognitive Search index that returns 403 without the API key embedded in their client, and their robots.txt disallows /svc and /kforcesvc. There is no clean way to support it.
